cards.existing: Aspirate is the easiest to spot – words start with `ch`, `ph`, or `th`. If you see those, the trigger is usually one of: `ei` (her), `tri`, `chwe`, `a`/`â`.

cards.existing: Welsh has multiple forms of 'the': `y` before consonants, `yr` before vowels, `'r` after vowels in the previous word. `Mae'r ci` vs `mae yr afal` (the apple is).

cards.existing: wedi + verbnoun = perfect tense. Dw i wedi bwyta (I have eaten). Replaces 'n from the present pattern.

cards.existing: Useful gender check: `ei` (his) triggers soft mutation, `ei` (her) triggers aspirate. `Ei gath` (his cat – soft) vs `ei chath` (her cat – aspirate).
